back: Edge/LB → API gateway (auth, validation, model alias) → quota and rate limiter → regional router → model cluster router → replica scheduler → GPU, with usage flowing back for billing and quotas.

front: Why charge rate limits on estimated tokens and reconcile later?
back: Output length is unknown at admission. Charge the estimate (prompt plus expected output) up front, then correct with actual usage when the stream ends.

front: Concurrent decoding streams from output tokens/s?
back: Little's law: streams = output tokens/s × TPOT. 2.08M tokens/s × 0.03 s ≈ 62,400.

front: What usually binds a replica's batch size: memory or latency?
back: Check both. KV memory gives one limit; a load test at the TPOT target gives another. Use the smaller (often latency).

front: Why is prefix-cache hit rate a capacity input?
back: Uncached prefill costs about 2 × parameters FLOPs per token. Dropping from 70% to 0% hits more than triples prefill compute.

front: Headroom to survive losing one of three regions?
back: Multiply the minimum by 3/2, then divide by the target peak utilisation (for example 0.8).
429: you exceeded your quota, honour retry-after. Overload: the service is out of capacity, back off with jitter or fail over.
Sheng et al., OSDI 2024: count weighted input and output tokens served per client and schedule the waiting client with the lowest count.
Pause batch, then queue or degrade low interactive tiers, protect paid interactive traffic last.

front: Why scope prefix caches per organisation?
back: A shared cache can leak through timing: a fast TTFT reveals someone recently sent the same prefix.

front: Why not round robin across LLM replicas?
back: It scatters conversations, so with N replicas a follow-up turn finds its cached prefix only about 1/N of the time.
Roughly expected cached tokens − λ × load, with a fallback to least-loaded above a load threshold so hot prefixes don't melt one replica.

front: Why does GPU scale-out take minutes?
back: Scarce GPUs, container pulls, loading hundreds of GB of weights (140 GB at 1 GB/s ≈ 140 s), CUDA graph capture and warm-up.

front: What turns headroom into useful work?
back: Preemptible batch or offline tiers that run on spare capacity and pause when interactive load rises.

front: Canary gates for a new model version?
back: Eval metrics (quality, refusals, format and tool-call validity) plus TTFT, TPOT and output length, compared with a warmed baseline.
nvidia-smi utilisation is the fraction of time any kernel ran. Goodput is requests per second meeting both TTFT and TPOT targets.

front: Cost of retrying a stream that failed at token 900?
back: Prefill of the whole prompt plus decoding all 900 tokens again (or the prompt plus 900 tokens re-prefilled if resuming).
The gateway keeps emitted tokens and on failure resubmits prompt plus those tokens to a healthy replica as a prefix, continuing the stream after a pause.
